## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 24) is a biographical poem preserved within the Therāpadāna of the Pali Canon [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. It recounts the meritorious deeds and karmic background of the elder (thera) Upavāna [Catalog; SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into five modern languages according to SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].

A striking feature of the text is its near-verbatim duplication within the Therāpadāna itself: SuttaCentral records a full parallel in the second *Upavānattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 562) [SuttaCentral]. This is confirmed by DharmaNexus, which identifies 55 shared matches covering nearly the entire poem (segments 0.2–53.4 aligning with 0.2–54.4 at 97% similarity) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral also documents passage-level parallels with the *Sāriputtattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 3) and the *Upālittheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 8), both of which are likewise detected as recurring formulas by DharmaNexus, alongside thematic resemblances to the *Maṇipūjakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 474) and the *Mahāvāṇijajātaka* (Ja 493) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

The verses of the text are heavily cited and commented upon in the Pali commentarial corpus, particularly in the *Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, where DharmaNexus identifies over one hundred matches across both its volumes [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language text-reuse analysis also detects alignments between the poem and non-Pali Buddhist literature, notably the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna*, the Tibetan translation of the *Vinayavastu*, and the Chinese *Saṃyuktāgama* (T 99) [DharmaNexus].
